security_audit.summary: Most detections are Markdown formatting, documentation links, or keyword terminology rather than malicious commands. The workflow executes an external package with paid API credentials, but its implementation was not included in the review.

remediation.issue: The external package and its credential handling were not included in the reviewed skill files.
remediation.suggestion: Review the pinned package and dependencies, document network destinations, and use restricted credentials.

content.value_statement: New AI products can create search opportunities that are difficult to prioritize. This skill organizes keyword candidates using demand, trends, and competition data.
actual_capabilities: Extract up to five product, model, tool, or repository names from supplied text.
Run a pinned new-term-radar release after the user approves the estimated cost.
Compare name and generic keywords using available volume, trend, and competition data.
Organize keyword decisions as prioritize, watch, or skip with short explanations.
Flag branded terms, failed sources, and limits in available trend estimates.
Summarize relevant markets, search results, and existing site actions when data is available.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10 or newer and the external new-term-radar package.
Requires an AIsa API key and paid lookups; the optional GoAnyAPI key adds data.
Search volume estimates are approximate and may lag by about two months.
Missing sources or credentials can reduce coverage and weaken trend readings.

use_cases.title: Prioritize content topics
use_cases.description: Compare emerging product names with related generic search terms before planning articles.

use_cases.title: Assess product opportunities
use_cases.description: Review demand, market data, and search competition for possible tools.

use_cases.title: Investigate market signals
use_cases.description: Extract new AI names from release notes or listening reports and rank their keywords.

prompt_templates.title: Research one name
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [AI product]. Estimate the cost and wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Compare product names
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare keywords for [name one] and [name two]. Include generic terms and explain each decision.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a market report
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract up to five recent AI product names from [text]. Tell me which names you selected and estimate the research cost.

prompt_templates.title: Plan search opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [names] and [repository mappings]. Compare relevant markets, page-one competition, and existing site actions when available.

output_examples.input: Research keywords for a new AI image detector.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies candidate product names, provides an estimated lookup cost, and asks for approval before running the research.

output: AI image detector: watch. The estimated demand is small and the available trend data is limited.
Product name: prioritize. Recent interest is rising, but the branded term may fade quickly.

best_practices: Provide specific product names or source text with recent release context.
Approve the estimated paid lookup cost before starting the external command.
Review source failures, branded terms, and estimate quality before making decisions.
anti_patterns: Treat estimated search volume as an exact count.
Assume a brief product-name spike represents lasting generic demand.
Treat missing source data as proof that a market has no demand.

faq.question: What input does the skill accept?
faq.answer: It accepts AI product, model, tool, or repository names, as well as text mentioning them.

faq.question: Does research cost money?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill estimates paid lookup costs and asks for approval before running.

faq.question: Which credentials are needed?
faq.answer: An AIsa API key is required. A GoAnyAPI key is optional and adds research data.

faq.question: How many names can be researched?
faq.answer: The instructions select at most five names for one research call.

faq.question: Are search volume numbers exact?
faq.answer: No. The reported daily demand is an estimate, and volume data can lag by about two months.

faq.question: Can the skill guarantee search rankings?
faq.answer: No. It reports available demand and competition signals, but rankings and outcomes are not guaranteed.
